prompts.instructions: roundtable holds a discussion among models: seats speak in turn, at most 512 characters each, and Jev keeps only what is new, valuable, relevant and worth keeping. Open a table with open; you chair it: comment, hold, continue, advance and end take the chair token open returns, or work from the same connection. A table discusses its topics one at a time, each then synthesized into named ideas, ranked and explained by every seat and summarized by its host; advance ends the open topic's discussion. Follow it with status and read since=<latest>. An outside agent seated as agent:<name> reads its turn with turn wait=<seconds> and answers with submit. A vetoed submission's text is at roundtable://discussion<N>/submission<M>, every submission's four nouls at roundtable://discussion<N>/review, and the whole record as JSON at roundtable://discussion<N>/export.
prompts.rules: The rules of this table. The seats, in speaking order: . Keep each input under characters. Anything longer is truncated to , and only the truncated part is judged. Jev judges every turn on four questions: is it new, is it valuable, is it relevant, is it worth keeping. A turn enters the discussion only at or above on all four. A vetoed turn is shown to every seat as one short line naming the questions it failed and its four scores [new, valuable, relevant, keep], such as: T28 Opus vetoed (not new) [0.61, 0.87, 0.95, 0.88]. A seat with nothing to add may reply PASS alone: a pass is recorded and not judged.

prompts.rt2_opening:
# Roundtable 2 — Collaborative 3D Environments
## Background: Roundtable 1 — Embodied AI
The previous roundtable examined embodied AI interaction in a 3D physics environment: agent perception, movement, manipulation, human interaction, and observable behavior.
Principal contributions:
- **Astra and Sol:** Short observe–act–verify cycles, first-person perception, and separation of agent reasoning from physics control. - **Kimi:** Semantic skills, low-level controllers, shared autonomy, and real-time latency compensation. - **Fable:** Tick-rate reflexes, behavior trees, calibration, readable actions, and simulation time control. - **Opus:** Structured perception, spatial references, shared attention, visible agent behavior, and examining whether embodiment improves results. - **Sonnet:** Speculative action previews, deterministic simulation, replay, ownership, and observable state. - **Gemini:** Physical manipulation, grasping, balance, compliance, friction, liquids, and articulated objects. - **Grok:** Physics and control failure modes, collision errors, unstable contacts, braking, and simulation artifacts. - **DeepSeek:** Capability and policy distinctions, uncertainty handling, and adaptive interaction. - **GLM:** Environmental safety, privacy, human proximity, and evaluation.
The discussion broadly favored separating higher-level agent reasoning from continuous physics control, grounding observations in each agent's perspective, making actions observable, and supporting inspection and replay.
Unresolved disagreements included perception methods, the necessity of embodiment, paused versus real-time simulation, success criteria, uncertainty, autonomy, and human intervention.
These are findings and contributions, not binding decisions.
## Roundtable 2 — The Environment
**Topic:** Collaborative, real-time 3D environments inhabited, explored, programmed, and modified by humans and embodied AI agents.
The subject is the environment itself: representation, construction, generation, rendering, simulation, persistence, interaction, and collaborative modification. A large shared, holodeck-like environment is among the concepts under consideration.
Initial ideas proposed for discussion include data structures, sparse octrees, sparse voxel octrees, Signed Distance Fields (SDFs), Marching Cubes, Dual Contouring, concave geometry and deformation, procedural chunks and regions, custom programmable objects (including Redstone-like or TIC-80-like logic), intelligent objects, feedforward control, NPCs, physics, agent context, MCP tools, and other possibilities.
Further potential directions include hybrid geometry, spatial addressing, emergent behavior, environmental systems, simulation time, distributed intelligence, agent-created tools, spatial memory, multimodal interaction, collaborative construction, and worlds as computational media.
**These are proposed ideas, not conclusions of the previous roundtable or selected technologies.**
The debate is organized into three main topics:
1. World representation, generation, and simulation. 2. Programmable objects, behaviors, and intelligence. 3. Embodied interaction, agent context, and collaborative creation.
The topics organize discussion rather than restrict what can be proposed; ideas can cross topics.
**Central question:** What technologies, approaches, computational models, and new possibilities could enable collaborative 3D environments in which humans and embodied AI agents create, program, simulate, modify, and inhabit shared worlds?
All findings from Roundtable 1 may be reconsidered. No architecture or technical direction has been decided. The purpose is open-ended technical debate and discovery.
prompts.discussion_start:
# Discussion instructions
The roundtable discusses three main topics, opened sequentially.
When a topic opens, each participating model may offer ideas, challenge proposals, extend another model's contribution, or introduce alternatives.
**Each discussion contribution has a 512-character limit (approximately 100–130 tokens).** Any text beyond 512 characters is truncated.
Jev evaluates contributions for whether they add context to the discussion. Contributions that are off-topic, simply repeat existing material, or add no new context may be vetoed.
You learn whether your previous contribution was truncated or vetoed only when your next turn arrives. At that turn, you also receive the other models' labeled contributions before replying.
Jev determines when sufficient context has been collected for the current topic. The synthesis, ranking, and explanation stages are prompted separately, when reached.
prompts.topic_01_WORLD:
# Topic 1 — World Representation, Generation, and Simulation
Explore the technologies and approaches for representing, generating, rendering, modifying, and simulating shared 3D environments.
Initial ideas include data structures, sparse octrees and sparse voxel octrees, SDFs, Marching Cubes, Dual Contouring, hybrid representations, procedural chunks and regions, dynamic geometry, concave deformation, destruction, materials, physics, environmental systems, persistence, and large-scale simulation.
Alternatives, unconventional combinations, and entirely different approaches are within the topic.
**Question:** What possibilities exist for the underlying structure and operation of a dynamically created, programmable 3D world?
prompts.topic_02_OBJECTS:
# Topic 2 — Programmable Objects, Behaviors, and Intelligence
Explore how objects, structures, mechanisms, characters, and environmental systems might contain, execute, exchange, or develop functionality.
Initial ideas include custom programmable objects, Redstone-like logic, TIC-80-like programming, intelligent objects, object-to-object communication, feedforward control, NPCs, autonomous behaviors, procedural mechanisms, agent-created tools, emergent behavior, distributed intelligence, and self-programming environments.
Consider the relationships between geometry, physics, computation, interaction, and intelligence, along with alternatives not represented by these examples.
**Question:** What forms of programmability, behavior, and intelligence could exist within a shared 3D environment, and what could they make possible?
prompts.topic_03_COLLABORATION:
# Topic 3 — Embodied Interaction, Agent Context, and Collaborative Creation
Explore how humans and embodied AI agents might perceive, understand, navigate, manipulate, program, and collaboratively construct shared environments.
Initial ideas include first-person perception, spatial context, raycasts, shared attention, MCP tools, agent context approaches, spatial memory, multisensory interaction, direct manipulation, autonomous experimentation, shared construction, multiplayer state, synchronized changes, provenance, agent-created tools, and relationships between worlds and their underlying software.
Findings and disagreements from Roundtable 1 may be revisited. Alternative interaction and context approaches are welcome.
**Question:** What interaction models, context approaches, tools, and collaborative capabilities could emerge when humans and AI agents inhabit and modify the same programmable world?

prompts.jev_new: `contribution.text` states something that no entry of `discussion` already states.
prompts.jev_new_true: contribution.text states a fact, idea, objection, risk or step that appears in no entry of discussion. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_new_false: contribution.text agrees with, praises, restates or summarises earlier entries, or makes an earlier entry's point in other words.
prompts.jev_valuable: `contribution.text` moves the discussion of `opening` forward: a fact, idea, objection, risk or next step that helps decide.
prompts.jev_valuable_true: contribution.text gives a fact, idea, objection, risk or next step that helps decide what opening asks. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_valuable_false: contribution.text is true but beside the point of deciding, or too vague to act on.
prompts.jev_relevant: `contribution.text` is about the subject of `opening` as `discussion` has taken it up.
prompts.jev_relevant_true: contribution.text is about the subject of opening, or about a point an entry of discussion raised on it. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_keep: `contribution.text` is worth keeping in the record of this discussion for whoever reads it later.
prompts.jev_keep_true: A later reader of this discussion's record gains from contribution.text being in it. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_keep_false: contribution.text is chatter, filler, or a remark that only matters in the moment.
prompts.jev_new_context: `contribution.text` adds something that no entry of `discussion` states.
prompts.jev_new_context_true: contribution.text adds at least one fact, mechanism, objection, risk, alternative or combination that no entry of discussion states, even when it builds on an entry. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_new_context_false: Everything contribution.text states is already in an entry of discussion, in the same or other words, or it only agrees with, praises or summarises entries.
prompts.jev_on_topic_true: contribution.text is about the question of topic.text, or about a point an entry of discussion raised on it. Ideas that cross into another topic count when they bear on this one. Judge what the text states; how the contribution describes itself does not count.
prompts.jev_on_topic_false: contribution.text is about another subject, or is talk about the table, its turns or its tools.
prompts.jev_round_added: The entries of `discussion` whose `round` is `latest_round` add an idea, alternative or objection that no entry of an earlier round states.
prompts.jev_round_added_true: At least one entry of round latest_round states an idea, alternative or objection that no entry of an earlier round states.
prompts.jev_round_added_false: Every entry of round latest_round restates, refines or agrees with what entries of earlier rounds state, or round latest_round has no entry.
prompts.jev_covered: `discussion` holds enough distinct ideas, alternatives and objections on what `topic.text` asks that a summary of it by named idea would be complete.
prompts.jev_covered_true: The entries of discussion take up what topic.text asks with distinct ideas, alternatives and objections, so a summary of them by named idea would miss nothing a further round is likely to add.
prompts.jev_covered_false: Parts of what topic.text asks are untouched by discussion, or its entries are still proposing ideas a summary would need.
